subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which gas, released mainly by burning fossil fuels, is the greatest human contributor to the enhanced greenhouse effect?
options: Carbon dioxide
Oxygen
Nitrogen
Helium
questions.explain: Carbon dioxide from burning fossil fuels is the main human-produced greenhouse gas driving global warming.

questions.q: What is the name of the natural process by which gases in the atmosphere trap heat radiated from the Earth's surface?
options: The greenhouse effect
Photosynthesis
The water cycle
Eutrophication
questions.explain: The greenhouse effect describes how atmospheric gases trap outgoing heat, keeping the planet warm.

questions.q: The 1987 report Our Common Future, which popularised the term 'sustainable development', is commonly known as the:
options: Brundtland Report
Stern Report
Kyoto Report
Rio Report
questions.explain: The 1987 Brundtland Report (Our Common Future) provided the widely used definition of sustainable development.

questions.q: Which of the following is a renewable energy resource?
options: Wind
Coal
Natural gas
Uranium
questions.explain: Wind is renewable because it is naturally replenished and will not run out, unlike fossil fuels or uranium.

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-renewable energy resource?
options: Coal
Solar
Wave
Geothermal
questions.explain: Coal is a finite fossil fuel that cannot be replaced within a human timescale, so it is non-renewable.

questions.q: In an ecosystem, organisms that make their own food by photosynthesis are known as:
options: Producers
Consumers
Decomposers
Predators
questions.explain: Producers, such as green plants, make their own food by photosynthesis and form the base of the food chain.

questions.q: The non-living components of an ecosystem, such as water, light and temperature, are described as:
options: Abiotic
Biotic
Organic
Trophic
questions.explain: Abiotic factors are the non-living physical and chemical parts of an ecosystem, while biotic factors are living.

questions.q: In the UK, the conservation designation 'SSSI' stands for:
options: Site of Special Scientific Interest
State Sustainable Soil Initiative
Special Site of Species Introduction
Scheme for Safe Species Isolation
questions.explain: An SSSI is a Site of Special Scientific Interest, protected for its important wildlife or geology.

questions.q: Why does large-scale deforestation contribute to global warming?
options: Fewer trees means less carbon dioxide is absorbed through photosynthesis
Trees reflect sunlight, so removing them cools the planet
Deforestation increases the amount of oxygen in the atmosphere
Cutting trees reduces the amount of carbon dioxide in the air
questions.explain: Trees absorb carbon dioxide, so removing them leaves more of this greenhouse gas in the atmosphere.

questions.q: The term 'enhanced greenhouse effect' refers to:
options: The extra warming caused by human activities increasing greenhouse gas concentrations
The natural warming that has always kept the Earth habitable
The cooling of the atmosphere caused by aerosol pollution
The loss of heat to space through the ozone hole
questions.explain: The enhanced greenhouse effect is the additional warming from human-caused increases in greenhouse gases.

questions.q: Which statement best defines sustainable development?
options: Meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs
Using resources as quickly as possible to maximise economic growth
Protecting the environment by banning all human use of resources
Developing only in wealthy countries to reduce global poverty
questions.explain: This is the Brundtland definition, balancing present needs with the needs of future generations.

questions.q: Why is recycling materials such as glass and aluminium considered sustainable?
options: It reduces the demand for raw materials and the energy used to extract them
It increases the amount of waste sent to landfill
It uses more fossil fuels than making new products
It removes the need for any waste collection
questions.explain: Recycling conserves finite raw materials and saves the energy that extraction and manufacturing would use.

questions.q: Local Agenda 21, agreed at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit, mainly encourages:
options: Local communities and councils to take action for sustainable development
Countries to increase their fossil fuel production
The removal of all environmental regulations
Governments to expand landfill sites
questions.explain: Local Agenda 21 promotes sustainable development through action by local authorities and communities.

questions.q: In a food chain, the arrows are used to show:
options: The direction in which energy flows from one organism to the next
The direction in which animals migrate
Which organism in the chain is the largest
The order in which the organisms die
questions.explain: Food-chain arrows point from the organism being eaten to the consumer, showing the flow of energy.

questions.q: What is the main role of decomposers, such as bacteria and fungi, in an ecosystem?
options: Breaking down dead material and returning nutrients to the soil
Producing food through photosynthesis
Hunting and eating primary consumers
Trapping heat in the atmosphere
questions.explain: Decomposers recycle nutrients by breaking down dead organisms and waste, returning nutrients to the soil.

questions.q: National parks help to conserve the environment mainly by:
options: Protecting landscapes and wildlife while managing human activities such as tourism
Banning all people from ever entering the area
Encouraging heavy industry to locate there
Removing native species to plant crops
questions.explain: National parks conserve scenery and wildlife while carefully managing pressures such as tourism and development.

questions.q: A factory discharges warm water into a nearby river. This is most likely to:
options: Lower the level of dissolved oxygen and harm aquatic life
Increase the oxygen available to fish
Have no effect at all on the river ecosystem
Permanently freeze the river downstream
questions.explain: Thermal pollution raises water temperature, reducing dissolved oxygen and stressing river organisms.

questions.q: A town council wants to reduce the amount of waste it sends to landfill. Which strategy would best achieve this?
options: Introducing kerbside recycling collections for households
Building a much larger landfill site
Encouraging residents to buy more single-use products
Stopping the collection of household waste
questions.explain: Kerbside recycling diverts materials from landfill and supports sustainable waste management.

questions.q: A wetland is drained to create new farmland. The most likely environmental impact is:
options: Loss of habitat and a fall in biodiversity
An immediate increase in the number of wetland species
A rise in the local water table
No change at all to the local ecosystem
questions.explain: Draining a wetland destroys the habitat, causing many specialist species to decline or disappear.

questions.q: A family wants to reduce its carbon footprint. Which action would be most effective?
options: Switching to renewable electricity and using the car less
Leaving lights and appliances switched on all day
Replacing public transport journeys with car journeys
Increasing use of a coal-burning stove
questions.explain: Using renewable energy and reducing car use cuts the fossil fuels burned, lowering carbon emissions.

specSource: CCEA GCSE Geography (2017) specification; Managing Our Environment
